claim: Choanoflagellates are the closest living relatives of animals.
source_text: Choanoflagellates, microscopic bacteria-eating eukaryotes that are the closest living relatives of animals
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by multiple citations (James-Clark 1868; Saville Kent 1880; Hibberd 1975; Carr et al. 2008; King et al. 2008; Ruiz-Trillo et al. 2008) and represents established scientific consensus.

claim: Some choanoflagellates have both solitary and multicellular stages in their life histories.
source_text: Moreover, some choanoflagellates have both solitary and multicellular stages in their life histories
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by citations to Leadbeater 1983; Karpov and Coupe 1998; Dayel et al. 2011.

claim: Algoriphagus machipongonensis induces rosette colony development in Salpingoeca rosetta.
source_text: Only one bacterial species from ATCC50818, the previously undescribed Algoriphagus machipongonensis (phylum Bacteroidetes; Alegado et al. 2012), induced rosette colony development in the RCA cell line
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by experimental data showing that A. machipongonensis was the only bacterial species out of 64 tested that induced rosette formation.

claim: No other co-isolated bacterial species is required to stimulate rosette colony development in S. rosetta when A. machipongonensis is present.
source_text: S. rosetta cultures fed solely with A. machipongonensis yielded high percentages of rosette colonies (Figure 1—figure supplement 1), demonstrating that no other co-isolated bacterial species is required to stimulate rosette colony development.
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by experimental data showing that monoxenic cultures with only A. machipongonensis produced high percentages of rosette colonies.

claim: All 15 members of the Algoriphagus genus tested were competent to induce colony development in S. rosetta.
source_text: All 15 members of the Algoriphagus genus (Table 1), as well as six other species in the Bacteroidetes phylum, were competent to induce colony development
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by experimental testing of 15 Algoriphagus species for morphogenic activity.

claim: Six other species in the Bacteroidetes phylum (non-Algoriphagus) were competent to induce colony development in S. rosetta.
source_text: All 15 members of the Algoriphagus genus (Table 1), as well as six other species in the Bacteroidetes phylum, were competent to induce colony development
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by experimental testing showing that 6 out of 16 non-Algoriphagus Bacteroidetes species induced rosette formation.

claim: No species outside of Bacteroidetes tested failed to induce rosette colony development.
source_text: In contrast, no species outside of Bacteroidetes and most of the non-Algoriphagus bacteria tested failed to induce rosette colony development
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by experimental data showing that 8 species from non-Bacteroidetes phyla did not induce rosette formation.

claim: RIF activity is present in conditioned medium from A. machipongonensis even when grown in the absence of choanoflagellates.
source_text: Preliminary studies demonstrated that RIF activity was present in conditioned medium from A. machipongonensis, even when grown in the absence of choanoflagellates.
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by experimental bioassay data showing that conditioned medium from A. machipongonensis cultures without choanoflagellates induced rosette formation.

claim: RIF activity is present in the A. machipongonensis cell envelope.
source_text: Furthermore, the activity was also found in the A. machipongonensis cell envelope
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by experimental data showing that cell pellet extracts from A. machipongonensis induced rosette formation.

claim: RIF activity is heat resistant.
source_text: Furthermore, the activity was also found in the A. machipongonensis cell envelope and was heat, protease, and nuclease resistant
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by experimental data showing that heat-killed A. machipongonensis and boiled conditioned medium retained rosette-inducing activity.

claim: RIF activity is protease resistant.
source_text: Furthermore, the activity was also found in the A. machipongonensis cell envelope and was heat, protease, and nuclease resistant
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by experimental data showing that proteinase K treatment did not eliminate rosette-inducing activity.

claim: RIF activity is nuclease resistant.
source_text: Furthermore, the activity was also found in the A. machipongonensis cell envelope and was heat, protease, and nuclease resistant
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by experimental data showing that DNase and RNase treatment did not eliminate rosette-inducing activity.

claim: The rosette-inducing compound is not a protein, RNA, or DNA.
source_text: revealing that the compound is not a protein, RNA, or DNA
evidence_reasoning: This claim is inferred from experimental data showing resistance to heat, protease, and nuclease treatments.

claim: Lipopolysaccharide (LPS) from A. machipongonensis does not induce rosette colony development.
source_text: Rosette colony development is induced by live A. machipongonensis and the sphingolipid-enriched lipid fraction (20 mg mL−1), but not by fresh medium, A. machipongonensis LPS (10 mg mL−1), PGN (50 mg mL−1), or LPS+PGN.
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by experimental bioassay data showing that purified LPS did not induce rosette formation.

claim: Peptidoglycan (PGN) from A. machipongonensis does not induce rosette colony development.
source_text: Rosette colony development is induced by live A. machipongonensis and the sphingolipid-enriched lipid fraction (20 mg mL−1), but not by fresh medium, A. machipongonensis LPS (10 mg mL−1), PGN (50 mg mL−1), or LPS+PGN.
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by experimental bioassay data showing that purified PGN did not induce rosette formation.

claim: The sphingolipid-enriched lipid fraction from A. machipongonensis induces rosette colony development.
source_text: Rosette colony development is induced by live A. machipongonensis and the sphingolipid-enriched lipid fraction (20 mg mL−1)
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by experimental bioassay data showing that the sphingolipid-enriched fraction induced rosette formation.

claim: RIF-1 has a molecular formula of C32H64NO7S.
source_text: Based on high-resolution mass spectrometry, RIF-1 has a molecular formula of C32H64NO7S (M-H: exptl. 606.44027, calcd. 606.44035
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by high-resolution mass spectrometry data.

claim: RIF-1 is a sulfonolipid with the structure 3,5-dihydroxy-2-(2-hydroxy-13-methyltetradecanamido)-15-methylhexadecane-1-sulfonic acid.
source_text: The RIF-1 structure, 3,5-dihydroxy-2-(2-hydroxy-13-methyltetradecanamido)-15-methylhexadecane-1-sulfonic acid, has two parts: a base (shown in red) that defines the capnine, and a fatty acid (shown in black).
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by detailed NMR spectroscopy (1D and 2D) and mass spectrometry data.

claim: RIF-1 represents only 0.015% of the A. machipongonensis sphingolipid pool.
source_text: RIF-1 represents only 0.015% of the A. machipogonensis sphingolipid pool.
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by quantitative analysis of the purification process yielding approximately 700 µg from 160 L of culture.

claim: Commercial sphingolipids (sphingomyelin, monosiloganglioside, galactocerebroside, and N-palmitoyl-DL-dihydrolacto cerebroside) do not induce rosette colony development.
source_text: Significantly, commercial sphingolipids (sphingomyelin, monosiloganglioside, galactocerebroside, and N-palmitoyl-DL-dihydrolacto cerebroside; Table 2) failed to show any activity in our assay system.
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by experimental bioassay data showing that these commercial sphingolipids did not induce rosette formation.

claim: RIF-1 is the first sulfonolipid demonstrated to influence developmental processes in eukaryotes.
source_text: To our knowledge, RIF-1 is the first sulfonolipid demonstrated to influence developmental processes in eukaryotes.
evidence_reasoning: This claim is based on the authors' knowledge of the literature and their experimental demonstration of RIF-1's morphogenic activity.

claim: Purified RIF-1 induces rosette formation with a bell-shaped dose-response curve over a broad range of concentrations, from 10^-2 to 10^7 fM.
source_text: Purified RIF-1 induces rosette formation with a bell-shaped dose-response curve over a broad range of concentrations, from 10−2 to 107 fM
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by experimental dose-response data shown in Figure 4.

claim: RIF-1 has extraordinary potency at femtomolar (10^-15 M) concentrations.
source_text: Here we show that a rosette inducing factor (RIF-1) produced by A. machipongonensis belongs to the small class of sulfonolipids, obscure relatives of the better known sphingolipids that play important roles in signal transmission in plants, animals, and fungi. RIF-1 has extraordinary potency (femtomolar, or 10 −15 M)
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by experimental dose-response data showing activity at femtomolar concentrations.

claim: S. rosetta can respond to RIF-1 over a broad dynamic range of nine orders of magnitude.
source_text: S. rosetta can respond to it over a broad dynamic range—nine orders of magnitude.
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by experimental dose-response data showing activity from 10^-2 to 10^7 fM.

claim: RIF-1 was detected in conditioned medium at a concentration of 80 ng L^-1.
source_text: The RIF-1 was detected in the conditioned medium at a concentration of 80 ng L−1.
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by LC/MS quantification data from conditioned medium extracts.

claim: The potency of RIF-1 signaling is comparable to that of silkworm moth sex pheromone signaling.
source_text: The potency of RIF-1 signaling compares favorably with that of silkworm moth sex pheromone signaling, in which vapors from an ∼4 fM solution of bombykol, the sex pheromone of the silkworm moth, induce a pronounced wing fluttering response in males
evidence_reasoning: This claim compares the experimental data on RIF-1 potency with cited data on bombykol pheromone signaling.

claim: RIF-1 is markedly more potent than other marine signaling molecules such as Vibrio autoinducer and Caribbean spiny lobster tripeptide pheromones.
source_text: the activity of RIF-1 at femtomolar concentrations makes it markedly more potent than other marine signaling molecules [e.g., Vibrio autoinducer (Schaefer et al. 1996) and the tripeptide pheromones of the Caribbean spiny lobster (Ziegler and Forward 2007)].
evidence_reasoning: This claim compares the experimental data on RIF-1 potency with cited data on other marine signaling molecules.

claim: S. rosetta and A. machipongonensis coexist in nature.
source_text: The ecological relevance of this signaling interaction is indicated both by the coexistence of S. rosetta and A. machipongonensis in nature
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the fact that A. machipongonensis was co-isolated with S. rosetta from the environmental sample ATCC 50818.

claim: Bacteroidetes bacteria regulate morphogenetic processes in diverse lineages including animals, red algae, and green algae.

evidence_reasoning: This is explicitly stated as a hypothesis and is speculative, though it references known phenomena in Bacteroidetes.

claim: Additional membrane constituents might be required for the full potency of RIF-1.

source_text: Therefore we favor a model in which A. machipongonensis cell density, as revealed by RIF-1 concentration, provides S. rosetta with an indication of conditions under which rosette colony development would be advantageous

source_text: for instance by promoting more efficient capture of planktonic bacteria (Kreft 2010).

claim: The ability of S. rosetta to respond to increasing bacterial cell density likely requires the hypothesized RIF-1 receptor to become less sensitive at higher concentrations.
source_text: In analogy to the chemotaxis system of bacteria (Falke et al. 1997), the ability of S. rosetta to respond to increasing bacterial cell density likely requires the hypothesized RIF-1 receptor to become less sensitive at higher concentrations.

claim: The high concentration cutoff in the dose-response curve reflects a complete loss of sensitivity at high, but non-physiological, RIF-1 concentrations.

claim: RIF-1 can function at a distance from A. machipongonensis cells.

claim: Bacterially-produced sphingolipids in general, and sulfonolipids in particular, may be essential for chemical signaling that allows Bacteroidetes to influence cell differentiation and morphogenesis in diverse animals.
source_text: The morphogenetic interaction described here between S. rosetta and A. machipongonensis raises the possibility that bacterially-produced sphingolipids in general, and sulfonolipids in particular, may be essential for the chemical signaling that allows Bacteroidetes to influence cell differentiation and morphogenesis in diverse animals
evidence_reasoning: This is explicitly stated as a possibility ('raises the possibility') and is speculative, extrapolating from the S. rosetta findings to broader animal biology.

claim: The RCA cell line was produced from ATCC50818 by serial treatment with chloramphenicol, ampicillin, streptomycin, and erythromycin.
source_text: The Rosette Colonies Absent (RCA) culture line was produced from ATCC50818 by serial treatment with chloramphenicol (68 μg mL−1), ampicillin (50 μg mL−1), streptomycin (50 μg mL−1), and erythromycin (50 μg mL−1)
evidence_reasoning: This is a methodological claim supported by the experimental procedures described.

claim: S. rosetta differentiates into a variety of cell types including attached thecate cells, solitary swimmers, rosette colonies, chain colonies and loose, disorganized associations of cells.
source_text: Under laboratory conditions, S. rosetta differentiates into a variety of cell types including attached thecate cells, solitary swimmers, rosette colonies, chain colonies and loose, disorganized associations of cells attached to one another at the collar or to bacterial biofilms
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by observational data and citation to Dayel et al. 2011.

claim: S. rosetta rosette colonies contain clusters of at least four closely associated cells with organized polarity, each cell oriented with its flagellum pointing outward from a central focus.
source_text: S. rosetta rosette colonies can be distinguished from other cell types in that they contain clusters of at least four closely associated cells with organized polarity; each cell oriented with its flagellum pointing outward from a central focus.
evidence_reasoning: This is a descriptive claim based on microscopic observations.

claim: Strain PR1 is most closely related to members of the Algoriphagus genus within the Bacteroidetes phylum.
source_text: comparison of the PR1 16S rRNA sequence to the Greengenes 16S rRNA database (DeSantis et al. 2006) revealed strain PR1 to be most closely related to members of the Algoriphagus genus within the Bacteroidetes phylum.
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by 16S rRNA sequence analysis data.

claim: PR1 was subsequently named Algoriphagus machipongonensis.
source_text: PR1 was subsequently named Algoriphagus machipongonensis (Bradley et al. 2009).

claim: Approximately 700 µg of RIF-1 was obtained from 160 L of A. machipongonensis culture.
source_text: From 16 L of A. machipongonensis culture, approximately 50 μg RIF-1 was obtained in sufficient purity. The entire process, from growth of the cells to isolation of pure RIF-1, was repeated nine times in order to obtain approximately 0.7 mg RIF-1 from a total of 160 L of A. machipongonensis culture.
evidence_reasoning: This is a quantitative claim based on the purification process described.
